**Triage: `needs-user-decision` + `domain:spec` + `target:v17`.**

## Classification

Not a defect card — it asks whether an accepted ADR's recorded decision stands or is superseded. Reversing (or ratifying the reversal of) ADR-0005's tenant-customizable whitelist is a public-contract call on the maintainer's desk, not something a dev agent may guess. Both routes the body lists are legitimate and they are mutually exclusive, so no dispatch is possible until the direction is picked. Filed to the decision inbox unchanged.

## Routing rationale (landing site, not title vocabulary)

`domain:spec`. The authoritative flag is `MetadataTypeRegistryEntry.allowOrgOverride` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts` (schema at :216, `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` entries at :604-:778) — verified on `origin/main`. Every listed route lands there: route 2 edits the flags directly, and route 3 ("whichever route is chosen") stamps the ADR id onto those same entries. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:6860` only *derives* `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES` from the flag, so it is a consumer, not the fix site. Per the skill's "shared contract surfaces have one owner", anything touching `packages/spec` belongs to the spec seat regardless of who needs it.

## Premise check — the drift is real, but the affected set is wrong in both directions

The body's claimed set ("8 types … object/field/flow/workflow/agent/permission/role/profile") is quoted from `packages/objectql/src/overlay-precedence.test.ts:19`, which describes the state at commit `ba252da0b`. That note has since gone stale. Measured against `origin/main` today, entry by entry:

| ADR-0005 says | live `allowOrgOverride` | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `object`, `field` ❌ | `false`, `false` | **no drift** — flipped back since `ba252da0b` |
| `hook` ❌ | `false` | no drift |
| `datasource` ❌ | `false` | no drift |
| `agent` ❌ | `false` | **no drift** — contra the body |
| `flow` ❌ | **`true`** | **DRIFT** (:649) |
| `permission` ❌ | **`true`** | **DRIFT** (:777) — the one security type still drifted |
| `tool`, `skill` ❌ | **`true`**, **`true`** | **DRIFT** — not named in the body |
| `page`, `app`, `action` ❌ | **`true`**×3 | **DRIFT** — not named in the body |
| `view`, `dashboard`, `report`, `email_template`, `translation` ✅ | `true`×5 | no drift |

Two corrections that change the card's scope before anyone prices it:

1. **The live drift set is 7 types — `flow`, `permission`, `tool`, `skill`, `page`, `app`, `action` — not the 8 the body names.** Three of the body's eight (`object`, `field`, `agent`) are already back to `false`; five of the live seven (`tool`, `skill`, `page`, `app`, `action`) are not in the body at all. The security exposure the body leads with ("three security types") is in fact **one**: `permission`. `role` and `profile` are not registry types (see 2).
2. **A second, independent staleness in the ADR itself:** `validation`, `workflow`, `approval`, `profile`, `role` appear in the ADR-0005 table but **do not exist in `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` at all** (full live type list: action, agent, api, app, book, dashboard, dataset, datasource, doc, email_template, external_catalog, field, flow, hook, job, mapping, object, page, permission, position, report, seed, skill, tool, translation, view). So the table names five types that were retired or never landed — whichever route is chosen, the amendment has to reconcile those rows too, not just the flags.
3. Also unlisted by the ADR while carrying `allowOrgOverride: true`: `dataset`, `book`, `position`. New types default to `false` per the ADR's closing rule, so these three are additions the table never recorded.

None of this changes the body's core claim — the reversal did happen without an ADR, Prime Directive #13 applies — but it shrinks the security surface, moves five types onto the list, and adds a table-vs-registry membership gap the body does not mention.

## Dedup

Full-text scan of all open issues and PRs across the three repos for `allowOrgOverride` / `ADR-0005` / `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES` / `ba252da0b`: no existing dispatch entry for this drift. Nearest neighbours are context, not duplicates — #6155 (the ruling whose main path rests on this card's outcome), #6190 (the concrete defect this gates), #5992 (ADR *numbering* ambiguity, a different governance defect). Cross-repo: nothing in objectui/cloud.

## Release board

`target:v17` on criterion ②: a published document declares seven types cannot be per-org overridden while the runtime accepts exactly those writes — declared ≠ enforced on a contract we ship. It also gates #6190, itself a v17 board item; a blocked blocker with no visible gate makes the board lie.

**Maintainer ruling — 2026-08-07.** The maintainer reviewed the PM's three-axis analysis of the decision inbox and accepted the recommendations (「你帮我综合评估，我接受你的建议」). Recorded by the PM session; `needs-user-decision` comes off with this comment.

**Decision: split the eight flipped types into two halves.**

1. **Revert to the ADR table — `allowOrgOverride: false` — for the six types with no argued case:** `workflow`, `approval` (automation row; `flow` is already ruled back to false via #6155 Q1=B, transfer card #6283) and `permission`, `role`, `profile` (the trio the ADR itself flags as "Authorization correctness; overlays would create silent privilege drift"). Include a migration assessment for any org-scoped overlay rows already stored under these types.
2. **`object` / `field` keep `true`** — the flip is the substance of project mode, i.e. real shipped pull — but the reversal must be legitimized by an **ADR-0005 revision section** that addresses the ADR's three named risks (physical schema divergence / execution side-effects / privilege drift) specifically for these two types. Until that section merges, the ADR remains the stated authority.

Both halves: leave the governing ADR id on the touched `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` lines and register them in `scripts/adr-anchors.json` — the reason this flip happened silently is that the edited lines named no ADR (PD #13 corollary).

Rationale: PD #13 — reversing a recorded decision is itself a decision needing an ADR; the split follows the evidence — object/field have a shipped feature behind them, the other six never received an argument.
